source_evidence: This is called “internalization.” In this way, your broker's firm may make money on the "spread" -- which is the difference between the price the firm paid for the security and the price at which the firm sells it to you.
answer: Internalization happens when your broker routes your order to another division of its firm, which fills the order using the firm’s own inventory. The firm may earn money on the spread: the difference between what it paid for the security and the price at which it sells it to you.
formula_latex: \text{Spread} = \text{price firm sells to you} - \text{price firm paid for the security}
